_about: Photogrammetry-style (AI) models of San Francisco landmarks: their source files and what tools/modelpack/pack.ts needs to make game-ready LODs of them. Intrinsic facts only (real size, which axis is the front, waterline, material); where a project puts one is that project's business (cityengine: public/landmarks/san-francisco-statues.json).

_fields.id: asset id in the assetkit-models-sf index
_fields.material: 'textured' (the file carries its own texture), else a shader for an untextured model: bronze (the default), copperoxide, concrete, whitestone, silver… (a material named in the file name wins)
_fields.front: the model's own axis its front faces, as the glTF loader leaves it: +z | -z | +x | -x
_fields.scale: { axis: x|y|z, metres }: the real size along that model axis; the whole model is scaled uniformly from it (a ship by its length, a statue by its height)
_fields.draft: ships: metres from the model's lowest point up to the waterline, after scaling
_fields.plinth: statues whose model has no base: the pedestal a renderer must draw, [width, depth, height] metres; absent when the model brings its own or stands on the ground
_fields.lods: levels to make: ratio of triangles kept (1 = all), texture cap in px, and the simplifier's error limit (fraction of the model's size; default 0.02 — a far LOD of a rigged ship needs more, or the thin lines stop it)
_fields.crop: optional { axis, max }: triangles whose middle is further than max (model units) from the centre along axis are dropped — a stray rope sticking out
_fields.squash: optional { axis, factor }: scale one axis only, for a model the AI stretched (the Pampanito came out twice as tall as she is)

models.name: Balclutha (1886 full-rigged ship)
models.description: Steel-hulled three-masted full-rigged ship built 1886 by Charles Connell & Co., Glasgow; museum ship of the San Francisco Maritime National Historical Park at Hyde Street Pier.
models.notes: Model length (z, 1.0 unit) runs from the bowsprit tip to the stern: 92 m overall (301 ft). The red bottom (antifouling) is about 8% of the length, and she floats light: in the 2012 photo (3-context.jpg) the upper part of the red shows, so the waterline is 4.5 m above the model's lowest point (2026-10-18). Her bow points toward the pier's shore end, by the Eureka (the same photo; about.md's 'north-west' is wrong). Two LODs only: the simplifier stops at ~8 k triangles whatever the error limit (the rigging is hundreds of separate textured strips with UV seams), and most of the memory is the texture; beyond lod1's range a game draws its own stand-in (cityengine: the procedural ship).

models.name: C.A. Thayer (1895 lumber schooner)
models.description: Three-masted wooden lumber schooner built 1895 by Hans Bendixsen, Fairhaven CA; museum ship at Hyde Street Pier.
models.notes: Model x runs over 67 m overall (219 ft, bowsprit and boom). A stray rope stood ~0.24 units out to the side (owner, 2026-10-18: 'may interfere with nearby objects'): cropped at |z| > 0.13 (the hull's half-beam is 0.084, deck fittings reach 0.12). Draft ~3.5 m (depth of hold).

models.name: Alma (1891 scow schooner)
models.description: Flat-bottomed San Francisco Bay scow schooner built 1891 at Hunters Point; museum ship of the San Francisco Maritime NHP.
models.notes: 18 m on deck; the model's z runs from the bowsprit tip past the boom, ~25 m. Its lowest point is the lowered leeboard, ~2.4 m below the hull, so the waterline (1.1 m draft) is ~3.5 m above it. Sails set, as Tripo made her.

models.name: Hercules (1907 steam tug)
models.description: Ocean-going steam tug built 1907 by John H. Dialogue & Son, Camden NJ; museum ship at Hyde Street Pier.
models.notes: 46 m (151 ft); draft 5.5 m aft, ~4.5 m mean.

models.name: SS Jeremiah O'Brien (1943 Liberty ship)
models.description: Liberty ship built 1943 at the New England Shipbuilding Corporation, South Portland, Maine; one of two operational Liberty ships, museum ship in San Francisco.
models.notes: 134.6 m (441 ft 6 in); laden draft 8.5 m, as a museum ship riding higher, ~6 m.

models.name: USS Pampanito (1943 submarine)
models.description: Balao-class fleet submarine launched 1943 at Portsmouth Navy Yard; museum ship at Pier 45, Fisherman's Wharf.
models.notes: 95 m (311 ft 6 in); surfaced draft ~4.6 m; the red bottom is below the waterline. Tripo made her 0.43 units tall to 1.0 long: 41 m at 95 m, against ~17-19 m keel to the top of the periscope shears; squashed in y by 0.47.

models.name: Taj Mahal houseboat, Sausalito
models.description: A houseboat in the form of a miniature Taj Mahal, Sausalito.
models.notes: An easter egg (owner, 2026-10-18). Size estimated (~14 m long on its float); its arched entrance is on -x.

models.name: Eureka (1890 paddle-wheel ferry)
models.description: Side-wheel walking-beam passenger and car ferry built 1890 (as Ukiah, rebuilt 1922 as Eureka); museum ship at Hyde Street Pier.
models.notes: 91 m overall (299 ft 6 in), 24 m over the guards; double-ended, so either end is its front. Model 'based on mini' (owner, 2026-10-18).

models.name: Victory, Dewey Monument
models.description: Bronze Victory with trident and wreath on a globe atop the Dewey Monument's column, Union Square (1903).
models.notes: Untextured: shade as copperoxide (named in the file). The on-site marker says 'twelve foot high bronze of Victory' (HMdb; Wikipedia's 9 ft is likely the figure without the raised arm). Figure ~3.7 m plus the globe ~0.9 m: 4.6 m overall. On the 85 ft column (cityengine draws it).

models.name: Mechanics Monument
models.description: Bronze group of five mechanics working a punch press, Market and Battery Streets (1901), honouring Peter Donahue.
models.notes: Untextured: bronze. The model carries the lower granite base; ~7.5 m overall.

models.name: Mahatma Gandhi, Ferry Building
models.description: Bronze striding Gandhi with his staff, at the Ferry Building (1988).
models.notes: Untextured: bronze. 8 ft (2.4 m) striding figure on its rough bronze base (Wikipedia, 'Statue of Mahatma Gandhi (San Francisco)'), on a block with a plaque raised on two steps — a long low block, wider than deep, in the Commons photo (drawn by the renderer).

models.name: Willie Mays, Oracle Park
models.description: Bronze Willie Mays at the swing, Willie Mays Plaza, Oracle Park (2000).
models.notes: Untextured: bronze. The model has its own thin base; on a granite pedestal ~1.5 m (drawn by the renderer).

models.name: Abraham Lincoln, City Hall
models.description: Seated bronze Lincoln on the Polk Street side of City Hall (1928).
models.notes: Untextured: shade as copperoxide (named in the file). Seated figure with chair and its base ~2.9 m, on a granite pedestal (drawn by the renderer).
